title: Customer Health QBR — Prep Guide & Facilitation Script
content:
Purpose:
This document is a compact, operational QBR prep guide and facilitator script focused on assessing customer health, surfacing renewal risk, and creating an actionable next-quarter plan. Its intended for CSMs running a 60-minute QBR with product and engineering partners on the call.

Quick primer: run the health scorecard and gather the dashboard links at least 5 business days before the meeting. If renewal is within 90 days, flag for an expanded renewal planning session.

Attendees (example):
- Customer: VP Product, Eng Manager, Program Lead
- Redwood: CSM (facilitator), Solutions Engineer (tech recap), AM/AE (commercial), Product/Eng (optional for roadmap deep-dive)

Pre-work to send 7 days before:
- One-page agenda + ask: 1) Add any pressing topics to the doc, 2) Provide top 3 success metrics they care about
- Request access or screenshots for internal dashboards if not already shared
- Share short survey (3 questions) to capture sentiment and major risks

Meeting agenda (60 mins)
1) 0:00-0:05 — Welcome & outcomes (CSM)
  - Script: "Thanks everyone. Well run through outcomes, a quick health snapshot, operational metrics, product roadmap items relevant to you, and close with prioritized actions and owners. Our aim is to leave with 3 clear next steps."

2) 0:05-0:15 — Customer context & wins (Customer first)
  - Script prompt for customer: "Please share the last quarters top wins, any shifts in focus or priorities for the coming quarter, and one area where you want Redwood to help more."
  - Note: CSM captures verbatim wins and priority shifts in meeting notes

3) 0:15-0:30 — Operational health snapshot (CSM + SE)
  - Metrics to show: API usage (tokens/day & trend), 95th/99th latency, error rate, embedding failures, cost per 1k tokens, quota throttles, SLA incidents
  - Script: "Well highlight whats improved, whats stable, and where we see anomalies. The goal: identify operational blockers that could impact your roadmap or costs."
  - Red flags to call out: rising error rate >0.5%, sustained latency >200ms at 95th, repeated quota triggers, spike in small short-lived calls (suspicious of inefficient prompting)

4) 0:30-0:40 — Quality & outcomes (Product/SE)
  - Review evals/quality regressions: prompt set performance, hallucination incidents, customer-facing bug tickets tied to model outputs
  - Script: "Heres where output quality is aligned with your SLAs and where weve seen drop-offs. We recommend these mitigations..."

5) 0:40-0:50 — Roadmap & capability alignment (Product rep)
  - Short product updates relevant to customer: upcoming kernel optimizations, new model variants, dedicated capacity options, improved observability hooks
  - Ask customer if any roadmap item should be prioritized for their use case

6) 0:50-0:58 — Prioritized actions & owners (CSM)
  - Capture 3 highest-impact actions with owner and due date. Example: "Run prompt audit (SE) — due 2025-03-01"
  - Quick renewal health check: current usage vs commitment, NPS/CSAT signals, exec sponsorship, open legal/infosec items

7) 0:58-1:00 — Close & next steps (CSM)
  - Script: "Thanks — well circulate the notes and action grid within 24 hours and propose dates for any follow-up deep dives."

Facilitation playbook (practical tips):
- Start 5 minutes early to check audio, screen share. Confirm roles (note-taker, timekeeper).
- Use the shared doc live: CSM edits the action grid during the meeting so everyone sees commitments.
- If a technical discussion runs long, offer a follow-up deep-dive and park it in the doc as a deferred item.
- Keep the conversation outcome-focused: push for decisions (who/when) rather than open-ended feedback.

Standard action grid template (to capture live) — use three columns in the doc:
- Action — short description
- Owner — name
- Target date — YYYY-MM-DD

Meeting prep checklist (internal, to complete 5 business days before QBR):
- Export usage & perf dashboards (last 90 days) and attach to QBR doc
- Run renewal health score: usage trend, cost delta vs committed, exec engagement, open tickets count, CSAT trend
- Collate top 3 customer success stories (case examples they can cite)
- Identify any outstanding legal/compliance blockers and owners
- Draft slide: "Top 3 opportunities for next quarter" (commercial / product / ops)
- Confirm attendee list & EOQ/renewal timeline; escalate to AM if renewal <90 days
- Prepare 1 demo or screenshot that illustrates a recommended improvement (e.g., new caching profile or prompt template)

Renewal risk signals (quick scan):
- Flat or decreasing usage for 2+ quarters without clear business reason
- Escalating ticket severity or repeated regressions
- Product team deprioritization or lack of executive sponsorship
- Unresolved compliance/security review items >30 days

Standard follow-up email template (to send within 24 hours):
Subject: Thanks — QBR notes & three next steps
Body: "Thanks for your time today. Attached are the slides and the live notes. Below are the three agreed actions with owners and due dates. If anything needs correction, please reply-all. Well sync again on [date] to check progress."

Appendix: Quick links to artifacts to attach in the doc (examples)
- Account scorecard dashboard URL
- Recent incident playbook (linked ticket)
- Prompt audit snippet (anonymized)

Notes-to-self (CSM rough items to fill in during prep):
- Customers top metrics (MAUs, revenue influenced, query volume per workflow)
- Known sensitive data concerns? (PII, regulated data flows)
- Recent cost surprises (unexpected token spikes): root cause hypothesis

Versioning & handoff
- Add a short changelog line at the top of the doc each time major edits are made (date, who, summary).
- After finalizing notes & action grid, set doc status to "final" and move follow-ups to the renewal tracker.

This guide is intentionally compact — use it as the runnable script for the live QBR and adapt per customer size and renewal timing.
